Here's a high‑level summary of this advanced Keras project using graph neural networks (GNN):

Project Title:
ai-ml-ds-GraphGAT-ExpFalco
File: graph_gat_node_classification.py

Short Description:
Implement a Graph Attention Network (GAT) in Keras using the Cora citation dataset for semi-supervised node classification. This version uses Spektral library for efficiency, multi-head attention, early stopping, GPU acceleration, and visualization of learned embeddings—significantly more advanced than standard dense or CNN models.

# graph_gat_node_classification.py

import numpy as np  # for arrays
import tensorflow as tf  # core TF
from tensorflow import keras
from spektral.datasets import citation
from spektral.layers import GATConv
from spektral.transforms import AdjToSpTensor
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.preprocessing import LabelBinarizer
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA

# Timestamp
ts: str = "2025-07-15T12:00:00Z"

# Load dataset
adj: np.ndarray
x: np.ndarray
y: np.ndarray
adj, x, y = citation.load_data('cora')  # x: node feats, y: labels

# Preprocess
adj = AdjToSpTensor()(adj)
LABELS = LabelBinarizer().fit_transform(y)
idx = np.arange(x.shape[0])
idx_train, idx_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(idx, LABELS, test_size=0.5, random_state=42)

# Model
N: int = x.shape[0]
F: int = x.shape[1]
n_labels: int = LABELS.shape[1]
X_in = keras.Input(shape=(F,), name='node_features')
A_in = keras.Input((N,), sparse=True, name='adj')

x1 = GATConv(8, attn_heads=8, activation='elu')([X_in, A_in])
x2 = GATConv(n_labels, attn_heads=1, activation='softmax')([x1, A_in])
model = keras.Model(inputs=[X_in, A_in], outputs=x2)
model.compile(optimizer=keras.optimizers.Adam(1e-3),
              loss='categorical_crossentropy',
              weighted_metrics=['acc'])

# Train
es = keras.callbacks.EarlyStopping(monitor='val_weighted_acc', patience=50, restore_best_weights=True)
history = model.fit([x, adj], LABELS, sample_weight=idx_train,
                    validation_data=([x, adj], LABELS, idx_test),
                    epochs=200, callbacks=[es], batch_size=N, verbose=2)

# Evaluate
eval_res = model.evaluate([x, adj], LABELS, sample_weight=idx_test, return_dict=True)
print("Test acc:", eval_res['weighted_acc'])

# Embeddings visualization
feat_extractor = keras.Model(inputs=model.inputs, outputs=model.layers[-2].output)
emb = feat_extractor.predict([x, adj]).squeeze()
Z = PCA(n_components=2).fit_transform(emb)
plt.figure(figsize=(6,6))
plt.scatter(Z[:,0], Z[:,1], c=y, cmap='jet', alpha=0.7)
plt.title("Node embeddings by true class")
plt.show()

🧠 Use Cases

  1. Node classification in citation / social networks
  2. Semi‑supervised learning on graphs
  3. Knowledge graph / molecule classification
  4. Dynamic graph adaptation (in follow‑up)

✅ Example I/O

Input: adjacency matrix + node features
Expected output: per-node softmax probability vector predicting paper class (e.g., 7 classes like „Neural_Networks“).
Quantitative test: model.evaluate returns weighted_acc ≈ 0.78–0.83

🔑 Key Learnings

  • GATConv (Spektral) with multi‑head attention
  • Semi-supervised training with sample weights
  • Embedding visualization + interpretability

  8. Monitoring: track drift, new citations
